principles: Use a single compatible language/locale source for a generated name unless the caller explicitly supplies another structure.

Do not infer race, ethnicity, religion, nationality, citizenship, gender identity, sexuality, personality, class, education, occupation, appearance, disability, relationships, values, or behavior from a name source.
Do not infer a name source from appearance, personality, work, education, wealth, hobbies, relationship style, pronouns, or gender identity.
Treat country and language inputs as routing constraints for name data, not as complete descriptions of a person.
Mark regional-language fallbacks honestly and never present them as exact country-specific coverage.
If a requested country has no compatible vetted pool, return an uncovered result rather than silently substituting an unrelated culture.

defaultBehavior.unspecifiedContext: choose one bundled source locale, then keep all automatically generated name parts inside that locale

notes: namePresentation is optional and never derived from a person's gender identity or pronouns.
Some source locales use an independent grammatical name form to keep inflected given/family/patronymic pieces internally consistent; that form is not treated as the person's gender identity.
Detailed mixed-heritage, diaspora, adoption, marriage, chosen-name, multilingual, and family naming histories should be authored as person facts rather than guessed from generated names.
